scenario_description: A hypothesis correctly cites real current-incident evidence (E1, so it survives) but ALSO cites a fabricated retrieved-context id 'K5' that was never shown (only K1 exists). The real parse_and_validate must strip K5 from supporting_context_ids and record the fabrication, while still keeping the hypothesis itself (since real evidence support is what gates retention, never context).

provenance.notes: Hand-constructed adversarial payload simulating a model that invents a K<n>/H<n> retrieval-context id, exercising Phase 6's own context-citation sanitization path (investigator_service.llm.validation.py).

ground_truth_rationale: A human reviewer confirms: this case's RetrievalContext contains exactly one real knowledge item (K1); 'K5' does not exist. Per llm/validation.py's own documented rule, a fabricated/absent context citation never gates a hypothesis's retention by itself -- retention is governed solely by real evidence support (E1, present here) -- so the hypothesis must survive with K5 stripped, not dropped entirely.
forbidden_outcomes: K5 surviving anywhere in the sanitized hypothesis
the hypothesis being dropped entirely merely because its context citation was fabricated, despite having real evidence support
